title: Map a PS2 mouse pointer and keep control of the emulator
summary: Enable pointer input only for a mouse-driven PS2 title, map the required buttons, test cursor capture safely, and keep a reliable route back to emulator controls.
heroAlt: A wireless computer mouse with a USB receiver.
author: EmuCore - Hub

blocks.text: PCSX2 treats mouse motion as a separate pointer input source that must be enabled before movement can be mapped. Its controller documentation warns that enabling the source hides the mouse cursor while emulation runs. A game can use pointer motion and mouse buttons alongside a regular controller, so map only the inputs listed by that game.

Before capturing the pointer, confirm the emulator pause or focus-release shortcut works. Save open desktop work, note the existing controller profile, and check the original game manual or control screen for which mouse buttons and motion behavior it expects. Avoid changing shared bindings if the title supports a per-game profile.

items: 1. Open Settings > Controllers and enable the Mouse/Pointer input source.
2. Select the intended PS2 port and map only the mouse buttons the game documents.
3. Map pointer motion after enabling its source; leave regular controller bindings intact if the game needs both.
4. Verify the pause or focus-release shortcut while the mouse pointer is visible.
5. Start at a menu or tutorial and move the mouse slowly to see whether the in-game cursor follows or the camera turns.
6. Pause, release focus, then repeat once after a cold restart.

blocks.text: The setup passes when motion produces the expected in-game response, each click triggers only its mapped action, and the verified pause or focus-release path restores desktop control. Check again after restarting: a mapping that works only in an old session may belong to an unassigned title profile.

items: Buttons work but motion does not: confirm Mouse/Pointer is enabled; button mapping alone does not enable motion.
The cursor disappears: use the pause or focus-release shortcut, then disable the pointer source in controller settings.
Aim moves too quickly: lower the title’s own sensitivity first, then change one mapping at a time.
Desktop hotkeys activate the game: inspect overlapping emulator and operating-system shortcuts before remapping controls.

blocks.text: Pause and close the title, disable Mouse/Pointer, and restore the recorded profile. Reopen a regular controller-driven game to confirm its inputs still work. If the pointer cannot be released, use the operating system’s normal app-switch or close command after saving desktop work; do not reset emulator data to clear an input binding.
